In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kinematical data favor Sgr as the parent of Pal 12, and that this event occurred ~1.7 +/- 0.7 Gyr.
, within the uncertainties, both the LMC and Sgr scenarios are viable, but the Sgr case seems to be slightly more likely.
Pal 12 was most likely captured by the Sagittarius dwarf spheroidal galaxy ~1.7 +/- 0.3 Gyr ago, although the LMC remains an intriguing and viable possibility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present kinematical evidence is consistent with the tidal capture of Pal 12 from the Sgr galaxy.
Pal 12's orbit is compatible with a scenario in which it originated from Sgr.
, within the uncertainties of our data and of the Sgr's orbit, the capture of Pal 12 by Sgr is a viable explanation for its young age.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the present data on Pal 12 and its host galaxy, Sgr, are consistent with each other, and the capture hypothesis is viable.
